page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor. This instance provides 8 shared vCPUs consisting of 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core running at 2.0 GHz, alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 8.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, featuring 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this server type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 4184.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 3103.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14019.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 33593.88, both falling in the average range. The system demonstrates strong memory performance, scoring 2959.37 on the PassMark memory test. In terms of LLM inference, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 448.64 tokens per second for small 135M models and a strong 33.46 tokens per second for medium 7B models, though performance drops to a weak 6.59 tokens per second for large 70B model prompt processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a balanced allocation of high-end GPU resources and system memory relative to its shared CPU configuration, making it a viable option for workloads that are heavily dependent on GPU acceleration rather than sustained multi-core CPU execution. The absence of local storage requires external storage attachments, which should be factored into architectural planning. This server is well-suited for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, image processing, ray tracing, and GPU-accelerated data science tasks.
